summary: Orchestrator jitter alignment causing periodic tenant 429s; request config guidance and short-term mitigation
description: Issue summary: Customer observes repeated waves of 429s between 00:00 and 00:15 UTC each day for their production ingest pipeline. Impact: user-facing webhook retries and delayed embeddings ingestion for the DataSleuth pipeline; spikes correspond to scheduled batch jobs and orchestrator-coordinated warmup tasks. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east with a reserved Dedicated pool; orchestrator runs ~1,200 short-lived workers across 24 pods that perform scheduled pulls and embed calls.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs daily scheduled job that launches 1,200 short-lived worker tasks during midnight UTC window.
2) Each worker performs a preflight health check (OPTIONS) then initiates 3 parallel embedding calls.
3) Orchestrator warmup flag set to true, and service-sidecanary path performs lightweight model warmup requests at the same time.
4) Observe 429s in client telemetry and on Redwood console token/quota dashboards.
observed_behavior:
- Sawtooth pattern of 429s starting at 00:00 UTC peaking at 00:03–00:07 and decaying by 00:15.
- Rate-limit headers show per-tenant token window exhaustion (X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0) with Refill-Interval anchored at top-of-minute.
- Logs show many simultaneous short-lived connections reusing ephemeral keys and healthcheck probes counted as requests.
- Customer noticed console shows 'burst_pool' credit approaching zero during the window.
expected_behavior: Scheduled background workers should not generate tenant-impacting 429s if burst credit and smoothing are configured for cron-style fanout; healthcheck probes ideally excluded from quota accounting or routed to a separate background pool.
logs:
[2026-03-12T00:02:01Z] ingress-proxy: src=10.8.2.14 tenant=ds-prod req=/v1/embeddings status=429 tokens=0 remaining=0 window_refill=60ms

[2026-03-12T00:04:45Z] console: burst_pool_credit=12 -> 0
comments: 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial report from customer attached; asked for telemetry screenshots and timestamps.
2026-03-12 - DataSleuth Support Rep (customer): Uploaded per-worker traces and confirmed orchestrator jitter was previously set to 0s. They confirmed >1k worker fanout at midnight UTC.
2026-03-12 - Marco Chen (SRE): Noted refill alignment looks suspicious; requested sampling from rate-limiter logs and tenant token refill metrics. Opened Slack thread #support-datasleuth.
2026-03-13 - Marco Chen (SRE): Found correlation between refill epoch boundaries and worker launch window; healthcheck OPTIONS counted as requests by edge; suggested immediate temporary mitigations.

2026-03-13 - Aisha Patel (Support): Shared short-term mitigation steps with customer and asked if they can stagger jobs while we validate configuration changes. Customer agreed to test a small jitter change.
2026-03-13 - DataSleuth (customer): Performed staggered rollout with 10s jitter and reported reduced peak 429s but still observed some soft throttles at peak concurrency.
investigation_notes: Sampled tenant refill logs show refill anchor at 00:00:00.000 and refill bursts every 60s with tokens slotted to tenant windows; large synchronous debit causes immediate exhaustion.
Healthcheck and preflight (OPTIONS) are currently accounted at the same priority as interactive embed calls in the customer's routing configuration.

Orchestrator warmup and canary paths fire lightweight model probing requests concurrently with worker launches; these are not tagged as 'background' in the customer's request headers so they consume primary burst pool.
Dedicated pool has burst_pool enabled but configured with low credit for background flows; smoothing interval is 60s and does not absorb the instantaneous fanout.
No sign of dedicated pool autoscaler failing; capacity adequate but token accounting is the limiter, not GPU saturation.
recommended_short_term_workarounds: Add randomized jitter (recommended 5–30s per worker) to scheduled job launches to avoid synchronized token drains.
Reduce preflight healthcheck frequency or mark preflight requests with X-Request-Purpose: background so they can be routed to a background-burst pool.
Temporarily increase tenant burst_pool credit for the midnight window via console (support-approved) while final config is validated.
Enable client-side exponential backoff with small randomized jitter for retry loops to avoid synchronized retry waves.
If using ephemeral keys, batch creation so not all workers create new keys at the same second (avoid credential churn double-counting).
recommended_long_term_changes: Configure route-level quota separation: isolate scheduled/background job routes to a distinct burst pool with larger smoothing window.
Adjust refill granularity: move from top-of-minute anchor to sliding refill or add micro-refills to avoid epoch alignment across tenants.
Enhance orchestration guidance in SDK: include helper to mark background calls and attach a recommended jitter helper for cron fans-out.
Consider server-side exclusion rules for lightweight model warmup probes or tag them as diagnostic and route to low-priority quota.
Add telemetry alerting rule: detect >50% of tenant debits within 30s window and auto-suggest staggered rollout to customers.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13: Agreed on a two-step plan with customer. 1) Short-term: DataSleuth added 10s jitter to job launches and reduced preflight to once per pod; Redwood Support temporarily bumped tenant burst_pool credits for two nights. Observed 70% reduction in peak 429 rate. 2) Long-term: SRE will onboard a route-separation config template for scheduled/background flows and open a follow-up internal ticket to evaluate sliding refill implementation. Customer satisfied with mitigation and will report back after full rollout.
next_steps:
- SRE (Marco Chen) to create internal follow-up INT ticket to prototype sliding refill (ETA 2 sprints).
- Support to follow up with DataSleuth on 48h observational window and close if no regressions.
- Document recommended cron jitter and background-pool config in public KB article.
